title: Rigveda 1.16: To Indra
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 1.16: To Indra: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 1.16 is a hymn of 9 verses addressed to Indra. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 1, a collection of hymns by many families of poets. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 8v-9r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 1.16.1-9 (aṣṭaka 1, adhyāya 1, varga 30); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 9r
translation.original_text:
1ā tvā̍ vahantu̱ hara̍yo̱ vṛṣa̍ṇa̱ṁ soma̍pītaye | indra̍ tvā̱ sūra̍cakṣasaḥ ||
2i̱mā dhā̱nā ghṛ̍ta̱snuvo̱ harī̍ i̱hopa̍ vakṣataḥ | indra̍ṁ su̱khata̍me̱ rathe̍ ||
3indra̍m prā̱tar ha̍vāmaha̱ indra̍m praya̱ty a̍dhva̱re | indra̱ṁ soma̍sya pī̱taye̍ ||
4upa̍ naḥ su̱tam ā ga̍hi̱ hari̍bhir indra ke̱śibhi̍ḥ | su̱te hi tvā̱ havā̍mahe ||
5semaṁ na̱ḥ stoma̱m ā ga̱hy upe̱daṁ sava̍naṁ su̱tam | gau̱ro na tṛ̍ṣi̱taḥ pi̍ba ||
6i̱me somā̍sa̱ inda̍vaḥ su̱tāso̱ adhi̍ ba̱rhiṣi̍ | tām̐ i̍ndra̱ saha̍se piba ||
7a̱yaṁ te̱ stomo̍ agri̱yo hṛ̍di̱spṛg a̍stu̱ śaṁta̍maḥ | athā̱ soma̍ṁ su̱tam pi̍ba ||
8viśva̱m it sava̍naṁ su̱tam indro̱ madā̍ya gacchati | vṛ̱tra̱hā soma̍pītaye ||
9semaṁ na̱ḥ kāma̱m ā pṛ̍ṇa̱ gobhi̱r aśvai̍ḥ śatakrato | stavā̍ma tvā svā̱dhya̍ḥ ||
translation.text:
1LET thy Bay Steeds bring thee, the Strong, hither to drink the Soma draught- Those, Indra, who are bright as suns.
2Here are the grains bedewed with oil: hither let the Bay Coursers bring Indra upon his easiest car.
3Indra at early morn we call, Indra in course of sacrifice, Indra to drink the Soma juice.
4Come hither, with thy long-maned Steeds, O Indra, to- the draught we pour We call thee when, the juice is shed.
5Come thou to this our song of praise, to the libation poured for thee Drink of it like a stag athirst.
6Here are the drops of Soma juice expressed on sacred grass: thereof Drink, Indra, to increase thy might.
7Welcome to thee be this our hymn, reaching thy heart, most excellent: Then drink the Soma juice expressed.
8To every draught of pressed-out juice Indra, the Vr̥itra-slayer, comes, To drink the Soma for delight.
9Fulfil, O Ṣatakratu, all our wish with horses and with kine: With holy thoughts we sing thy praise.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 9r (OPenn image 10, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 1.16.1 ‹-soma-pītaye indra tvā sūra-cakṣasaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 9v, begins in RV 1.17.3 ‹ā tā vām nediṣṭham›. Verses 1.16.1-9 end on this page; 1.16.1 begins on fol. 8v.
